To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the elliptic flow of hadrons in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and LHC is well described in a hydrodynamic model, with initial conditions obtained from the Monte-Carlo KLN model, and that a saturation of elliptic flow is not observed in the energy range 7.7 ⩽ s A GeV ⩽ 2000.

(a) elliptic flow of charged hadrons is found to saturate in the s range of 39 ⩾ s ⩾ 2760 AGeV, and that (b) this saturation is due to the interplay between elliptic flow and radial flow, and (c) this saturation is absent for MC-KLN initial condition with η / s of 0.2.
the energy dependence of the differential charged hadronic elliptic flow v2ch(pT,s) exhibits a broad maximum in the energy region 39 ⪉ s ⪉ 2760 AGeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the hydrodynamic evolution of a heavy ion collision from the lowest to highest energy.
a comprehensive study of the energy dependence of hadronic observables from RHIC to the LHC.
the study of the energy dependence of the azimuthal anisotropic flows in the framework of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a fixed initial condition, the elliptic flow is a monotonically increasing function of the fluidʼ s entropy production, and thus of the fluidʻs viscosity.
the elliptic flow data at RHIC and LHC can not distinguish between different initial conditions.

the elliptic flow v ch 2 and the spatial eccentricity e x on the freeze-out surface are both found to increase with s for MC-KLN initial condition, but decrease with s for MC-Glauber initial condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the elliptic flow v ( p T ) is a good probe to study the QGP fluidʼs shear viscosity at different collision energies, while the spatial eccentricity e x ( s ) is a good measure to study the initial spatial eccentricity at different energies.
the elliptic flow is saturated at RHIC energies for both MC-Glauber and MC-KLN model initial conditions, but it is still rising at LHC energies.
the initial eccentricity of the fluid plays an important role on the evolution of the fluid and its subsequent hadronization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the s -dependence of elliptic flow is a sensitive probe of the fluidʼ s viscosity, which can be used to test and constrain models for initial-state fluctuation.
the elliptic flow of hadrons is not only sensitive to the initial spatial anisotropies of the fluid, but also to its shear viscosity.

the s -dependence of the flow anisotropy coefficients v 2 ch and v 3 ch can be understood in terms of a simple hydrodynamic scaling relation which depends only on the initial spatial eccentricities e x and e y of the system.
